name: Enzalutamide
route_note: oral capsules or tablets 160 mg once daily, usually with ongoing androgen deprivation
originator: University of California, Los Angeles (Charles Sawyers, Michael Jung); developed by Medivation and Astellas

discovery.by: Charles Sawyers and Michael Jung, UCLA
discovery.note: Designed from the non-steroidal scaffold RU59063 to bind the androgen receptor with high affinity and no agonist activity when the receptor is overexpressed.

tagline: Androgen receptor blocker that extends survival across stages of advanced prostate cancer
summary: Enzalutamide is an oral androgen receptor inhibitor that blocks androgen binding, nuclear translocation and DNA binding of the receptor. It extends survival in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer and is approved across non-metastatic, hormone-sensitive and biochemically recurrent disease.
mechanism: Castration-resistant prostate cancer often remains dependent on androgen receptor signalling through receptor overexpression or intratumoral androgen synthesis.

Enzalutamide binds the ligand-binding domain with several-fold higher affinity than bicalutamide and inhibits three steps: androgen binding, nuclear translocation of the receptor, and binding of the receptor to DNA and co-activators. Unlike first-generation antiandrogens, it shows no agonist activity in receptor-overexpressing cells.
uses: Non-metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer with high-risk biochemical recurrence
Combination with talazoparib in HRR-mutated mCRPC

history.title: Discovery
history.detail: Sawyers and Jung identify MDV3100 at UCLA (published in Science, 2009).

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Approved after AFFIRM for mCRPC previously treated with docetaxel.

history.title: PREVAIL
history.detail: FDA extends use to chemotherapy-naive mCRPC.

history.title: Pfizer acquires Medivation
history.detail: Pfizer acquires Medivation and co-commercialises Xtandi with Astellas.

history.title: ARCHES
history.detail: Approval for metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer.

history.title: EMBARK
history.detail: Approval for non-metastatic castration-sensitive disease with high-risk biochemical recurrence; talazoparib combination also approved.

pk.metabolism: hepatic CYP2C8 (to active N-desmethyl enzalutamide) and CYP3A4; strong CYP3A4 inducer

facts: As a strong CYP3A4 inducer it lowers levels of many co-administered drugs.
